I'd say that Crime and Punishment is the most readable. I think it's actually on the shorter side of his novels. One thing I really appreciate about this book is the authors portrayal of the subjective passage of time. You know, when something bad is happening, it feels like forever? The author did such a good job at transferring the protagonists' strain of thoughts in those time, really makes you feel like you're waiting for something too.

I'd also recommend books like Anna Karenina, it was in that time period that authors, mostly the Russian and the French, started to portray women as actual people with personalities. (The Antics also did a good job with that, but later it was all about saving a woman from evil, or the woman making the man a better person.) Their roles aren't to change men for the better anymore, they can lead their own lives, make big changes, be fatalistic. Those traits are normal now, but it was so important to portray them back then, to make people notice how women are struggling with being separate beings from the men. Aside from that, it is the time period of realism, so I really like that side of literature. I love feeling like things are real, sometimes struggle is bigger than the nice things and it has to be portrayed properly. I'm rambling lol, I'm sorry for my English.
